newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis, NIH collaborate on transplants.
newsitem.headline: Novartis, NIH collaborate on transplants.

text.p: Novartis AG said on Monday it had signed a collaborative research and development agreement and a worldwide licensing agreement with the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH) for anti-CD3 immunotoxin.

Novartis Pharma, a unit of the Swiss Life Sciences group, said anti-CD3 immunotoxin utilises an experimental treatment called 'tolerance induction', which attempts to teach the body to accept a foreign organ as its own.
The current standard for transplant recipients is immunosuppresive therapy, which prevents rejection of transplanted organs by suppressing the body's natural immune response.
Pre-clinical trials with anti CD3 immunotoxin have resulted in the development of stable tolerance for the transplanted kidney in a high percentage of animals studies, Novartis said.
Although these results are preliminary and years away from potential human applications, Novartis said they are among the best results to date for tolerance induction in higher primates.
